content.text: Plan Your Trip to Outer Banks: Best of Outer Banks TourismOuter Banks, North Carolina Save this place to a Trip, where you can track your faves and get personalized picks as you plan.The Outer Banks of North Carolina is a 100-mile stretch of barrier islands dotted with pristine beaches, quaint towns and historic sites. If you love swimming, kayaking, or surfing, be sure to visit the Cape Hatteras National Seashore. To really experience local culture, explore each coastal village and sample as much food as you can along the way. (Pro tip: Try the catch of the day.) If you’re looking for a history lesson, check out Roanoke Island or the Wright Brothers National Memorial. And of course, no day is complete without watching the sunset from Jockey’s Ridge.Discover your perfect Outer BanksLooking for places to stay, eat, or explore?Essential Outer BanksPick a category to filter your recsThings to doWhen to visitJanuaryModerately busyBusiest monthMayVery busyLeast busy monthAugust9 days of rainWettest monthItineraries to help you planCreated by AI, guided by insights from our community. Learn moreTrending in the forumsOuter Banks Is Great ForShopaholicsLocal eatsAfter darkExplore more from our sponsorsBest cities to visit in Outer BanksOuter Banks travel tipsThese questions and answers were created by AI, using the most common questions travelers ask in the forums.Activities and SightseeingMany travelers recommend exploring the natural beauty and historical sites of the Outer Banks. Popular activities include visiting the Wright Brothers Museum, Jockeys Ridge for sand dune climbing, and taking wild horse tours in Corolla. Additionally, the Cape Hatteras National Seashore and Bodie Island Lighthouse are must-see destinations for their scenic views and historical significance.Wildlife and Outdoor AdventuresFor wildlife enthusiasts, travelers have suggested trips to the Pea Island Wildlife Refuge for birdwatching and nature walks. Kayaking and stand-up paddleboarding are also popular activities, with Kitty Hawk Kites mentioned as a provider for these services.Local Culture and Historical SitesExploring local towns like Manteo is recommended, where visitors can enjoy quaint shops, waterfront parks, and historical attractions like the Roanoke Island Festival Park. The Lost Colony outdoor drama is a cultural highlight during the summer months.Beach ExperienceAccording to forum posts, spending time on the beaches is a key part of the Outer Banks experience. Places like Coquina Beach, known for its undeveloped landscape and fewer crowds, are particularly appealing. Evening walks on the beach to hunt for ghost crabs and enjoying sunsets at Jockey’s Ridge are cherished activities.This summary was generated by AI from Tripadvisor forum posts. Beach and Nature ExplorationSome travelers recommend visiting the Bodie Island Lighthouse and taking walks on the boardwalk over the marsh. Coquina Beach, known for its undeveloped landscape and fewer crowds, is also suggested for a peaceful beach day. The Pea Island Wildlife Refuge is another spot for nature lovers, offering a visitor center and paths around the refuge.Historical and Cultural SitesAccording to forum posts, families enjoy exploring Manteo, where they can visit the Roanoke Island Festival Park for a historical experience. The town's boardwalk and the Island Bookstore, with its extensive collection on local history and nature, are also popular. Additionally, the North Carolina Aquarium is a favorite for its outdoor nature trail and exhibits.Active and Educational ActivitiesTravelers have called out Jockey's Ridge State Park as a must-visit for flying kites and watching sunsets. An airboat eco-tour with Outer Banks Adventures offers both fun and educational experiences, guided by certified environmental educators. For a unique experience, a wild horse tour in Corolla provides an opportunity to see the horses in their natural habitat.Leisure and Night ActivitiesFor relaxed evenings, walking on the beach with flashlights to hunt for ghost crabs is a fun activity that children particularly love. Some users also suggest simply enjoying the local ice cream as a sweet end to a day of adventures.This summary was generated by AI from Tripadvisor forum posts. Traffic CongestionAccording to forum posts, traffic in Corolla, part of the Outer Banks, can be quite challenging, especially on weekends. Some travelers have highlighted that the main roads into and out of Corolla experience high congestion, particularly on Saturdays during peak vacation periods, as this is a common turnover day for rentals.Alternative Traffic DaysTravelers have suggested planning arrivals or departures on non-peak days to avoid the worst of the traffic. Some users pointed out that weekday traffic is significantly better compared to weekends, which can help in scheduling activities and excursions more smoothly.Local AdviceExperienced visitors recommend exploring Corolla and surrounding areas during the week to mitigate the impact of traffic delays. This approach allows for a more enjoyable experience when accessing local attractions and beaches.This summary was generated by AI from Tripadvisor forum posts. Reputable AgenciesAccording to forum posts, several rental agencies in the Outer Banks have been praised for their service. Twiddy, Resort Realty, Joe Lamb, and Village Realty are frequently mentioned for their reliability and positive rental experiences.Additional OptionsFor those considering alternatives, some travelers suggest exploring direct rentals from owners through platforms like Facebook groups, notably OBX VACATION HOME RENTALS BY OWNERS. This option may provide personal service and direct communication with property owners.Cautionary AdviceHowever, some users have advised caution with certain agencies due to negative experiences. Stan White Realty, particularly dealing with specific staff members, has been called out for poor communication and management, especially during the check-in process.This summary was generated by AI from Tripadvisor forum posts. Transport ServicesAccording to forum posts, travelers have utilized coastal transportation for reasonably priced trips between Norfolk Airport and OBX, though specific details on service quality are limited. Additionally, OBX First Watch is highly recommended by users for transport from Kitty Hawk to Norfolk International Airport, praised for prompt responses and pleasant service. Contact information for OBX First Watch includes their phone number, 252-256-9617, and website, www.obxfirstwatch.com.Ferry OptionsSome travelers expressed interest in using ferries as a scenic and potentially time-saving alternative. However, the practicality of ferry use depends on the exact locations within OBX and the ferry schedules. Specific route advice was not detailed, but the general consensus suggests that driving may be more efficient for direct travel between Norfolk and OBX without the logistical constraints of ferry timings and reservations.This summary was generated by AI from Tripadvisor forum posts. Vehicle RequirementsAccording to forum posts, driving on the beaches of the Outer Banks requires a 4x4 vehicle, and all-wheel drive (AWD) vehicles are not recommended due to the soft sand. It's essential to air down the tires to about 18 psi to improve traction.Permits and RegulationsSome travelers mentioned that a permit is necessary for beach driving and parking on certain beaches. For instance, Corolla/Carova beaches require a permit for parking, but not for driving. The National Park Service (NPS) manages permits for other areas, and these can be purchased online.Environmental ConsiderationsTravelers have called out the environmental impact of beach driving. It's important to observe designated areas to protect wildlife, including sea turtles and nesting birds. NPS rangers reportedly check beaches daily for environmental compliance before allowing vehicles.Time RestrictionsDriving on the beach is often restricted during certain times of the year to protect local wildlife and manage tourist traffic, as noted by users discussing regulations on various OBX beaches.This summary was generated by AI from Tripadvisor forum posts. Fireworks and Radio BroadcastSome travelers mentioned that Hatteras Island hosts an annual Independence Day celebration with fireworks launched from Avon Pier. The event includes a patriotic music broadcast by Radio Hatteras.Fishing OpportunitiesAccording to forum posts, Hatteras Harbor is a popular spot for booking fishing charters, with options for nearshore and inshore fishing, offering a chance to enjoy the local aquatic life.Driving and Bonfires on the BeachTravelers have called out that Hatteras National Seashore permits driving on certain beaches with a permit, and bonfires are allowed in designated areas with a beach fire permit, enhancing the outdoor adventure experience.Museum VisitsFor those interested in history, the Graveyard Museum of the Atlantic in Hatteras Village is recommended. It recently reopened and features unique exhibits like an actual Enigma machine from WWII, providing a cultural and educational outing.This summary was generated by AI from Tripadvisor forum posts. Please read full forum posts for more details and information.Frequently Asked Questions about Outer BanksIf you're a more budget-conscious traveler, then you may want to consider traveling to Outer Banks between December and February, when hotel prices are generally the lowest. Peak hotel prices generally start between June and August.
